source.rule: All narrative presence, names, aliases, locations and movements in this analysis are extracted only from the Internet Archive transcription. External sources are not used to establish novel facts.

title: Earth

movement_status_legend.confirmed: The text explicitly establishes the character at the destination or explicitly describes the completed movement.
movement_status_legend.intended: The text describes a destination or direction of travel, but does not yet establish arrival.
movement_status_legend.relative: The text establishes a relative movement/location relation without enough information for a precise route.

confirmed_movement_points.evidence: The pair reaches the wooded hills and spends two days foraging in the hollows of Mount Ibuki.
They move at night in what they think is the direction of the small town of Tarui; this passage does not by itself establish an arrival at Tarui.
They are taken in and concealed at Oko and Akemi's house after reaching it as sick stragglers from Sekigahara.
Takezo goes into the nearby mountains with Akemi to collect supplies and encounters Temma.
Takezo returns to the house after the mountain encounter.
Otsu spots Takezo among the crowd outside Shippoji during the flower festival; he immediately disappears.
Takezo is hiding in the Sanumo mountains while search parties pursue him.
Takuan takes Otsu into the mountains and uses the surrounding terrain while waiting for Takezo rather than conducting a conventional search.
Takezo approaches their camp/fire and is captured by Takuan.
Takuan brings the captured Takezo back to Shippoji.
Takezo is tied to the old cryptomeria tree in the temple grounds.
Takezo is freed and escapes with Otsu; the text explicitly has them reach Nakayama Pass before separating.
Takezo continues toward Hinagura to find Ogin; the narrative subsequently places him at the Hinagura stockade area.

Otsu agrees to go to Himeji and wait at Hanada Bridge; this is an intended destination and later sections establish her route through the Hanada/Mikazuki area rather than treating the initial promise as immediate arrival.
The narrative brings Takezo into the Himeji area after the Hinagura sequence.
Takuan brings Takezo before Lord Ikeda Terumasa at Himeji Castle.

identity_checkpoint.evidence: At Himeji Castle, Ikeda asks for Shimmen Takezo's name and the later naming scene establishes Miyamoto Musashi.
identity_checkpoint.spoiler_rule: The canonical identity remains the same internal character ID; only the reader-facing identity changes at the narrative point where the new name is established.

notes: This file is an analysis layer, not yet the final map database.
Movement status was refined during the primary-text audit: direction/intention is no longer treated as confirmed arrival.
Locations and movement edges will be normalized against the location registry before UI integration.
No future-book information is used to establish Book I presence.
